parts:
Dear Kat,

 

What were your values of lambda and p and the sample sizes that you were using ? And did you use the NegBin binomial Nmix models for estimation ?

 

You may have small sample bias in the estimates and for some binomial Nmix models, the parameters may not be estimable, which may show up as high abundance estimates that only a finite value of K keeps from getting infinity, as they are in reality (see paper by Dennis et al in Biometrics in 2015).

 

Best regards  -- Marc

 

 

 

Von: unma...@googlegroups.com [mailto:unmarked@googlegroups.com] Im Auftrag von K Womack
Gesendet: Montag, 1. Mai 2017 15:52
An: unmarked
Betreff: [unmarked] N-mixture models for removal sampling using PCOUNT overestimating abundances from simulated data

 

Hi UNMARKED Google Members,

 

I simulated data to evaluate the performance of the n-mixture model for repeated visits and the multinomial Poisson model with removal sampling to test the utility of both models for bat ecological studies. I ran multiple scenarios – varying sample size (number of sites), number of visits, and probabilities of detection and population sizes.

 

I found that overall the n-mixture model overpredicted abundances for most of my simulated datasets, whereas, the removal sampling model was accurate in predicting the population size for most variations within a scenario.

 

I did not include covariates in either model, as I wanted to understand how both preformed without additional factors that would affect abundance estimates.

 

Does anyone have a possible explanation why this is happening? Or has anyone else found similar results?

 

Thank you all for your time,

 

Kathryn
